newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: No job cuts seen at Renault in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: No job cuts seen at Renault in Portugal.

text.p: Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said on Tuesday he did not expect French carmaker Renault to cut jobs in Portugal in 1997 following its announcement that it planned to shut a plant in Belgium.

"The agreement (between Renault and the Portuguese government) establishes that throughout 1997 Renault will create jobs that permit the attainment of an average level of employment identical to 1996," Mateus told TSF radio.
Two plants produce Renault cars in Portugal, located in Setubal south of Lisbon and Cacia in the centre of the country.

Last June the government signed a deal with Renault under which the carmaker handed over control of the Setubal factory to a Portuguese state company, guaranteeing that the plant would continue producing Clio saloons until July 31, 1998.

Renault announced on February 27 that it would close the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, which employs 3,100 people, in July as part of a programme to reorganise and streamline its European car assembly operations.
